name: Treaty with the Wea, 1809 (Vincennes convention of October 26, 1809)
nations: Wea (now part of the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: The Wea gave their full consent to the Fort Wayne treaty of September 30, 1809 with the Delaware, Miami, Potawatomi and Eel River, and to the separate article made that day with the Miami and Eel River.
In return for the Wea relinquishment under the first article of the Fort Wayne treaty, the United States agreed to an additional annuity of $300 and a payment of $1,500.
The United States agreed to a further permanent annuity of $100 to the Wea once the Kickapoo consented to the ninth article of the Fort Wayne treaty.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the Wea held 549,081 acres in the western part of Royce Area 71 and were paid for their interest under this treaty of October 26, 1809: a $300 permanent annuity (commuted value agreed at $6,000) and $1,500, $7,500 in all. It found the Wea land worth $686,400, about $1.25 an acre, on January 16, 1810, held the consideration so grossly inadequate as to be unconscionable, and awarded $678,900 to the Peoria Tribe on behalf of the Wea.

landTaken: 549,081 acres in the western part of Royce Area 71 in Indiana, held by the Wea (Indian Claims Commission, 22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 92, 1969).
compensation: At the time, a $300 permanent annuity and $1,500, which the Commission valued at $7,500 in all. On November 26, 1969 the Commission awarded $678,900 for the Wea lands in Area 71 to the Peoria Tribe on behalf of the Wea (Docket 314-D). Whether it was paid has not been traced.
today: The Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma brought the Wea claims as successor to the Wea Nation.

nationVoice.nation: Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nationVoice.summary: The Tribe's history counts the Wea, a subtribe of the Miami Nation, among its founding peoples and says that some Weas joined the confederation led by Tecumseh and the Prophet in the early 1800s, that at St. Mary's, Ohio they ceded most of their lands in Indiana, Illinois and Ohio, and that, having disposed of all their lands, the remaining Wea moved west; it does not discuss the 1809 convention itself.

openQuestions: Audit 2026-11-08 (round 11): rewritten for the Wea convention of October 26, 1809 only (7 Stat. 116, Royce area 71), as treaties.json now records it. Removed the Fort Wayne material: Article 9 and the Area 73 strip, the Docket 314-C findings (OSU id 2276) and $349,750 award (OSU id 1048), the Miami and Eel River award, and the Kickapoo Tribe in Kansas testimony. Those are noted on kappler-109 (Fort Wayne, which now carries area 73) and belong with kappler-112 (Kickapoo) for the testimony.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 11): the remaining breach is tied to this treaty by the Commission itself: its finding 64 (22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 92, OSU id 2096, re-opened) says the Wea consideration for Area 71 was the $300 annuity and $1,500 of the Treaty of October 26, 1809. The final award (OSU id 2633) lists $678,900 for Docket 314-D, Royce Area 71, dated November 1969 (day illegible; the collection gives November 26).

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 11): the $100 annuity promised here on the Kickapoo's consent to Article 9 was the Wea consideration for Area 73; the Commission held that consideration unconscionable in Docket 314-C (22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 186, 1969; final award $349,750, 1970). Because Area 73 is the Fort Wayne treaty's Article 9 cession, that finding is recorded with kappler-109, not counted here.
A Peoria Tribe or Wea statement on this treaty was not found.

plain.promised: The Wea agreed to the Fort Wayne land cession of 1809. The United States promised them a $300 yearly payment and $1,500, and $100 more a year once the Kickapoo agreed.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1969 that the Wea were paid $7,500 for 549,081 acres worth $686,400, and held that unconscionable.
plain.today: The Commission awarded $678,900 in 1969 to the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma on behalf of the Wea. Whether it was paid has not been traced.
